steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat pumpkin, sugar, oil, and eggs together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until well combined.
Sift flour, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a separate large bowl.
Stir flour mixture into pumpkin mixture until no dry streaks remain.
Spread batter evenly in an ungreased 10x15-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Remove cake from the oven; let cool before frosting.
Beat butter and cream cheese together in a medium bowl until smooth; stir in vanilla extract. Gradually add confectioners’ sugar, beating until frosting is smooth.
Spread frosting evenly on cooled cake. Cut into 24 bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Paul’s Pumpkin Bars
raw_recipe.description: These moist pumpkin bars are warmly spiced with cinnamon and topped with smooth cream cheese frosting for an easy fall dessert that serves a crowd.

review.reviewBody: These are a bit "cakey" for me - here is how I modified them to be PERFECT - and people at work obsess over them! I put in only 3 eggs, then instead of 15 oz of pumpkin, I put in a 30 oz can of pumpkin pie mix (I use Libby's). I then add an additional teaspoon of pumpkin pie seasoning to the flour mix, in addition to the cinnamon. I've got my baking time down to 27 minutes in my oven, which is just the point where the toothpick comes out clean for the first time. Then for the frosting, I add 8oz cream cheese, and double the rest of the frosting ingredients. PERFECT!

After reading the other reviews, I decided to try for a more bar-like result for today's picnic. I cut out one egg and ½'ed the baking powder and baking soda. I also added ½ tsp. of cloves and ½ tsp. of nutmeg. I thought they turned out great!! VERY moist, and exactly like I wanted. For the frosting, I used 8 oz of cream cheese and 3 cups of powdered sugar, which made about ½ cup more than I needed. A GREAT recipe!

I loved ease and delicious results. I cooked my own pumpkin (2 cups packed) and pureed it in my vitamix heavy duty blender with the 4 eggs and then added the other wet ingredients. i replaced oil, with 1 cup melted butter and I added 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and additional pumpkin pie spice and powdered ginger, 1 teaspoon each. I still added the cinnamon to the dry ingredients and sifted them together. I replaced white flour for whole wheat white flour, and added 1 extra teaspoon baking powder to compensate. I also added 1 package chocolate chips at end before pouring into the jelly roll pan. I used 1/2 sheet size and found it filled the pan nicely. I doubled all the cream cheese frosting ingredients and found this allowed for generous layer. I topped my bars with gold sparkly dust and walnut halves. This was for Thanksgiving, so all upgrades were taken. It was a great recipe to adjust to personal liking.

Excellent, just as I remember them from growing up. Moist, fluffy and wonderful! They are more of a "cake" but it is the "title" I used when searching for the ones I remembered from childhood. I made exactly as directed except subbed 1 3/4 cup pureed pie pumpkin for 15 oz can. Also, baked in 9x13 for almost 45 minutes. Yummy! I might spread out the batter between two pans for a "smaller bar"

I used CIRCEKITTY'S changes. It was exactly what I wanted, more bar like- not cake. I added a TBS of vanilla. I only had pumpkin filling, so I generously added 3 tsp of Penzey's pumpkin spice. OMG! these were so delicious!

I followed a few of the reviewers suggestions because just cinnamon was not enough spice for me. Added a tsp of pumpkin pie spice and extra 1/2 cup of pumpkin. Needed to cook about 15 minutes longer than asked. Super moist still. The icing was sooooo sticky and couldn't taste the cream cheese. Added another 3 oz. and a 1/4 cup of heavy cream to make it spreadable. The final product was sooooo good! 5 stars after the adjustments.

I have made this recipe multiple times. We love it! Like others suggested, I used only 3 eggs but 2 cans of pumpkin. I also added a lot more spices (additional cinnamon, ground cloves, ginger, and nutmeg). For the frosting, I used 8 oz. cream cheese and doubled the rest of the ingredients. I baked it for 27 minutes in a 1-inch deep jelly roll pan of the suggested size. It turns out a very moist cake bar...a real treat.

EPIC recipe! I gave 5 stars because it is very good without any frosting, (which my son's teacher doesnt like the kids getting at school.) I used 1/2C applesauce & 1/2C oil, instead of the whole C of oil, & added 1 tsp Pumpkin Pie spice. Instead of frosting, I sprinkled chopped walnuts on 1/4 of the pan, which worked out Awesomely. -Perfect crunch texture for adults! I will definitely be making this again-TY!!

The best cake I've ever had...can't believe I MADE IT!!! It's so moist and fluffy and the perfect amount of sweet-I used less sugar.
The substitutions I made were:
Less sugar-About 1 1/3 C
Homemade pumpkin puree (used more than 15oz)
Used 1/2 C olive oil 1/2 C Apple sauce 
Only 1C confectioners sugar 
And creamed by hand since I don't have mixer
Will certainly make this again!

This recipe was fantastic! If I could give it more than five stars, I would! Here are the small changes I made: I used 4 jumbo eggs (instead of 4 large eggs) because that’s what I had on hand. I think the jumbo eggs made it a bit more like cake which my family loved! In the future, if I don’t have jumbo eggs, I would probably use 5 large eggs. I also added a tablespoon of vanilla to the batter and would do this again. For the frosting, I melted the butter, added an extra cup or so of powdered sugar and added some vanilla. It was perfect. I sprinkled chocolate chips on top of the frosted cake. It was delicious! I have honestly never made a pumpkin anything that got so many compliments!

We also tweaked this a bit and had luscious results. Used 2 cups gluten free flour, entire 30 oz can of pumpkin, reduced sugar to 1 1/4 cup, reduced oil to 1/2 cup, added 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder to dry ingredients and 1 cup chocolate chips to batter. Swirled 1/3 cup melted chocolate over top of bars before baking and what came out of the oven after 30 minutes was exactly what we'd hoped for. Nicely firm pumpkin bars with lovely touches of gooey chocolate! Have used a tweaked version of Sally's Baking Addiction pumpkin bars for years but this rivals our old recipe and we'll definitely make it again (sorry, Sally, and we still love ya!). UPDATE: Have now made these without any chocolate added but still gluten free with reduced sugar and oil (added applesauce in place of the reduced oil) and get rave reviews every time. Perfect for church potluck and you will get "hallelujah-amens!"

Surprised but not surprised to see this recipe still around. Made it 20 years ago, for office parties, they were a huge hit then. And looks like they still are. Yes, the original "Paul's pumpkin bars", and if there really is a Paul, kidos @!!!
I absolutely love making these in the fall or really any time of the year. They are phenomenal! The cake is super most and fluffy, and the frosting gives it the perfect touch!

I've made this and changed it up almost every time. It's a good recipe but it can be changed up easily as well. Sometimes I add raisins, or ground cloves or even chai tea works great. I have even make a plain icing or the one my family prefers:- a maple flavored icing.
I added the spices listed on the can of pumpkin puree for pumpkin pie and that's just what it tastes like.
the pumkin bars wher i good treat for thanksgiving

I’ve made these as written and they are good. I just tried to make them more like bars by using 2 eggs and half the baking soda and half the baking powder. They turned out a bit denser but still very good. For the frosting I just used ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter softened (113g) 8 oz cream cheese softened (brick-style, not spreadable) (226g) 1 teaspoon vanilla extract ¼ teaspoon salt 4 cups powdered sugar* (500g) Taste test after each cup of confectionery sugar, so it’s your perfect level of sweetness.
Everyone absolutely loved this recipe. Instead of 2 teaspoons of cinnamon, I used 1 and 1/2 teaspoons of cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice! Yum!
I made this twice and twice it was nothing but an oily mess… I think there’s too much oil in it. I’m hoping that’s a misprint because the mess is awful.
Yummy
